newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after strong ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called higher after strong ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open higher Friday, led by a stronger ACCESS session and early talk of stronger cash prices, industry sources said.
July over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.10 to $2.12 after settling Thursday at $2.08 per mmmBtu.
On ACCESS, July last traded 2.5 cents higher at $2.105.

"Everything appears to be up three cents. You're starting to get some heat. The heat index in Houston yesterday was 102 (degrees F)," one trader said, noting heavy utility buying has propped up Henry Hub cash.
Technical traders pegged July resistance at $2.135, and then at $2.15-2.16. Further resistance was seen at $2.21 and $2.25. Traders said support was at $2.08, and then at $2.

In Thursday's cash, swing gas at the Louisiana Gulf was talked a couple of cents lower in the low-teens. Midcon pipes lost a few cents to the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas lost similar ground to the high-$2.30s.

Weather was expected to remain moderate throughout most of the U.S. into early next week, Weather Services Corp reported, with slightly above-normal temperatures forecast to blanket most of the South.
